content: To determine if lansoprazole is suitable for you, it is important to discuss your current and past health conditions with your healthcare provider. Inform them if you have any of the following conditions: low blood potassium levels (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium levels (hypocalcemia), low blood sodium levels (hyponatremia), liver problems, or phenylketonuria. Lansoprazole may interact with other medications and supplements. Before starting lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are taking. For more details, refer to the interactions section. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. It is not known if lansoprazole can affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. Your provider will advise you on whether you should take lansoprazole during pregnancy or while trying to conceive. Do not take lansoprazole while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Lansoprazole should be taken before meals. It is unclear if alcohol consumption affects lansoprazole. Always inform your healthcare provider about any medications or supplements you are using, especially if you are taking methotrexate, digoxin (used for irregular heartbeat or heart failure), warfarin (a blood thinner), theophylline (for lung diseases), clarithromycin (an antibiotic), tacrolimus (to prevent organ transplant rejection), certain antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir for HIV/AIDS), St. John’s Wort, or rifampin (for tuberculosis). Some medications may alter the blood levels of lansoprazole or vice versa. Always provide a complete list of medications to your healthcare provider. If you or someone else accidentally takes too much lansoprazole, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of lansoprazole, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Common side effects of lansoprazole include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, and constipation. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, though less common, include kidney problems (e.g., acute tubulointerstitial nephritis), antibiotic-associated diarrhea (e.g., Clostridioides difficile infection), severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), a severe allergic reaction called DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms), lupus, vitamin B-12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, and bone loss or fractures. If you experience symptoms such as decreased urine output, blood in urine, watery diarrhea, severe stomach cramps, fever, rash, joint pain, or changes in heart rate, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Lansoprazole should not be used by individuals allergic to its ingredients, including those in Prevacid, Prevacid SoluTabs, Prevacid 24HR, or other proton pump inhibitors. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in specific lansoprazole products. Do not take lansoprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Take it as directed and do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep it out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush lansoprazole capsules. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents on one tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Swallow the mixture immediately without mixing it with other foods. If given through a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow your healthcare provider’s instructions. Lansoprazole SoluTabs contain phenylalanine, a component of aspartame. Children under one year of age may be at greater risk for certain side effects. Discuss the risks with your healthcare provider if your child is under one year old. Lansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to fully work. If you are also taking sucralfate, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate. Antacids may be taken with lansoprazole if needed. This information is provided for general educational purposes. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most current and personalized advice.
